newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack faces government reprimand - paper.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack faces government reprimand - paper.

text.p: British railway operator Railtrack Plc is expected to face a public reprimand on Thursday from Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott over the company's excessive profits, said The Guardian newspaper.
Prescott will tell Railtrack that it should no longer put the well-being of shareholders above those of the taxpayer, said the newspaper.
Analysts expect the company to report a near 60 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 300 million sterling for the year to March 31, due to be announced Thursday.

Britain's Labour government has threatened a tougher regulatory regime for Railtrack following sharp criticisms by the industry regulator Ofrail that the company was lagging behind in its spending promises.
Railtrack is also in the line of fire for the government's proposed windfall tax on excessive profits made by privatised utilities.
